security_audit.summary: Twenty alerts are false positives involving Markdown backticks, readable multilingual text, public HTTPS requests, a comment, and provider identifier matching. Five filesystem alerts reflect predictable shared temporary files that permit symlink overwrites or cache tampering when another local user can pre-create them. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Downloads and Python examples use predictable shared temporary paths for writes and subsequent reads.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with mktemp -d or tempfile.TemporaryDirectory. Keep downloads and reads inside it, avoid pre-existing paths, and remove it afterward.

content.value_statement: Finding reliable contact details for Taiwan medical providers can require searching multiple sources. This skill guides searches using the public NHI-contracted provider directory.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve public NHI-contracted provider records without an API key or login.
Download directory records through offset pagination with up to 1,000 records per request.
Filter providers by name, address prefix, and provider type.
Report provider names, addresses, telephone numbers, and directory classifications.
Guide related service-hour and department lookups using provider identifiers and the dataset catalog.
Explain source failures and distinguish directory records from real-time clinical information.
limitations: Cannot provide live queue progress, appointment booking, doctor schedules, or temporary closure updates.
Directory updates can lag openings and closures; representative addresses may not identify every branch.
Address filtering does not calculate distances or guarantee the nearest provider.
Requires network access and local command execution; related datasets and query filters require verification.

use_cases.title: Find a clinic contact
use_cases.description: Search a district or provider name and obtain directory contact details before calling.

use_cases.title: Prepare a provider list
use_cases.description: Collect providers by city and type for a contact list, while preserving source addresses and directory classifications.

use_cases.title: Research provider coverage
use_cases.description: Retrieve paginated public records and compare provider categories across cities without treating directory counts as real-time availability.

prompt_templates.title: Look up one provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the NHI directory contact details for [provider name]. Report its name, address, telephone number, and source.

prompt_templates.title: Filter a local directory
prompt_templates.prompt: List [provider type] providers in [city or district] using NHI directory records. Include contact details and preserve original addresses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: filter by location and type

prompt_templates.title: Check listed service hours
prompt_templates.prompt: Find [provider name], then use its HOSP_ID to check listed Saturday service hours. Distinguish fixed hours from temporary closures.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a complete directory extract
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve all NHI provider records using offset pagination. Use a private temporary directory, compare fetched counts with result.total, and summarize [city] providers by type.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: retrieve and validate a full directory

output_examples.input: Can this directory show the current queue number or book an appointment?
output_examples.output: No. The directory provides provider contact details, not live queue status or appointment booking. Contact the provider directly.

best_practices: Preserve full-width address characters and representative-address labels when reporting source records.
Check pagination totals and query-filter behavior before claiming a result list is complete.
Use a private temporary directory and confirm important visit details directly with the provider.
anti_patterns: Treating directory entries or fixed service hours as proof of current availability.
Assuming one large limit request returns the complete directory.
Inventing provider contact details when the source request fails.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The documented NHI open-data endpoints require neither an API key nor a login.

faq.question: Which providers are covered?
faq.answer: The directory covers NHI-contracted providers, including hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, and nursing institutions. It is not a directory of every healthcare business.

faq.question: Can it book appointments or show live queues?
faq.answer: No. Appointment booking, live queue progress, and doctor schedules are outside its scope.

faq.question: Can it check Saturday service hours?
faq.answer: It describes matching providers to the fixed service-hour dataset through HOSP_ID. Confirm temporary closures and current hours directly with the provider.

faq.question: How does it retrieve the full directory?
faq.answer: It uses offset pagination because the documented API caps responses at 1,000 records. Total counts can change between updates.

faq.question: What should happen when the API fails?
faq.answer: The skill recommends retrying with a browser User-Agent and reporting source failure when necessary. It should not invent contact details.
